name: Arbitrary-Company Stability and Data Layer

phase_requirement_check.requirement: Freeze a reproducible blind-test baseline before execution and preserve the first output, errors, warnings, and diagnostics without replacing the issuer.
phase_requirement_check.evidence: ODFL remains the deterministic S05 issuer; its 22 first-run artifacts pass the immutable SHA256 registry.

phase_requirement_check.requirement: Harden quarter, YTD, FY, LTM, instant/flow, units, currency, shares, non-calendar years, 53-week years, negative denominators, and missing XBRL tags in the shared Data Layer.
phase_requirement_check.evidence: S06 owns these rules in build_public_company_decision_pack.py; the Investment Layer delegates to the shared selectors instead of recreating them. Nineteen dedicated tests pass.

phase_requirement_check.requirement: Harden debt maturity, revolver, covenant, lease, receivable, bad debt, supplier finance, acquisition, amendment, restatement, and subsequent events without silently resolving source conflicts or stale information.
phase_requirement_check.evidence: S07 exposes eleven modules through one shared version 1.1.0 contract. Twenty-five dedicated tests and the ITT forward-test history pass.

phase_requirement_check.requirement: Rerun CROX, AZO, first blind companies, and a newly selected unfamiliar company; verify safe outcomes and absence of company-specific analytical branches.
phase_requirement_check.evidence: CROX, AZO, ODFL, and ITT all pass the final live acceptance with zero Hard Stops; synthetic safe failures and AST anti-hardcoding checks pass.

scope_boundary: Phase B acceptance applies to the current SEC-reporting, US-GAAP, non-financial public-company core.
MISSING and WARNING are accepted only as explicit constrained outcomes, not as evidence that the missing disclosure exists.
Future live fixtures for distressed, restated, material-event, and complex-capital-structure issuers remain additional coverage.
exact_next_starting_point: Read and freeze the approved S09 definition before implementing Phase C.
